CORRECTIONS REQUIRED
An audit of the extractions against Pieter K. Baaij’s Paulus als Schriftuitlegger: Paulus’ vertolking van Genesis 15:5b-6 in Romeinen 4:3 (2005) confirms that all extracted claims and section locators are strictly supported by the text, but identifies three technical adjustments needed to fix garbled OCR text in quotations and preserve the author's precise grammatical nuances.
Itemized Audit Findings & Corrections
1. Correction of Garbled Characters in Quotation (Check #2)
Location: Section 3 (Passage 29).
Previous Extraction: Quoted S07F-E002 as "de . om het voorafgaande [werk]woord extra nadruk te verlenen..."
Source Observation: The OCR text rendered the Greek postpositive conjunction δέ as a period artifact (de .). In the original source text, Baaij writes: *(Grieks: δέ om het voorafgaande [werk]woord extra nadruk te verlenen én om aan te geven dat hij meer aspecten aangaande dit gebeuren [‘vertrouwen’] gaat vermelden...)* [Passage 29].
Correction: Update quotation in S07F-E002 to read: "*Grieks: δέ om het voorafgaande [werk]woord extra nadruk te verlenen...*" [Section 3, Passage 29].
2. Exact Grammatical Qualification of τῷ θεῷ as Causal Dative (Check #6)
Location: Section 3 (Passages 30, 33).
Previous Extraction: Characterized πιστεύω τῷ θεῷ in S07F-E003 simply as a dative without preposition indicating the Initiator.
Source Observation: Baaij explicitly specifies that he translates τῷ θεῷ as a causal dative (dativus causae) meaning "omwille van deze God" ("on account of / because of this God"), highlighting that God's spoken promise is the divine cause that evokes Abraham's trust [Passage 33].
Correction: Refine claim S07F-E003 to include Baaij's specific German/Dutch grammatical translation: Paul uses πιστεύω with a simple dative (τῷ θεῷ), which Baaij interprets as a dativus causae and translates as "omwille van deze God" ("on account of this God") to emphasize God as the active cause of Abraham's trust [Section 3, Passages 30, 33].
3. Normalization of OCR Beta-Code Transcriptions in Quotations (Check #2)
Location: Section 3 (Passage 30).
Previous Extraction: Quoted S07F-E007 with raw OCR Beta-code strings ("Paulus gebruikt immers niet pis, teuw evpi, cum dativo...").
Source Observation: In the printed PDF, Baaij uses Greek font characters (πιστεύω ἐπί cum dativo in Rom 9:33; 10:11; πιστεύω cum accusativo in Rom 4:5, 24; πιστεύω cum dativo without ἐπί or εἰς in Rom 4:3) [Passage 30].
Correction: Normalize the quote in S07F-E007 to standard Greek typography: "*Paulus gebruikt immers niet πιστεύω ἐπί cum dativo (zoals in Rom. 9:33; 10:11)... Hij gebruikt hier πιστεύω cum dativo zonder ἐπί of εἰς*" [Section 3, Passage 30].
Audit Verification Across the 7 Audit Checks
Direct Source Support (Check #1): Verified. All claims regarding Genesis 15:5b–6 and Romans 4:3 correspond directly to Baaij's Dutch text.
Quotation Accuracy (Check #2): Addressed in Items 1 and 3 above.
Observed Printed Page Numbers (Check #3): Verified. Because printed page numbers are not present in baaij_2005_romans_4_3.pdf, all locators were explicitly designated as UNKNOWN (Section X / Passage Y), strictly adhering to Check #3 without inferring page numbers.
Possibility vs. Certainty (Check #4): Verified. Baaij's explicit conditional premise—that his thesis assumes Paul's Hebrew Vorlage did not deviate from the Masoretic Text (Passage 13)—was properly retained as a qualification.
Scholar Attribution (Check #5): Verified. Baaij's interaction with Van Unnik (Passages 8–11), Cranfield/Fitzmyer (Passage 13), Meijering (Passage 32), and Den Heijer (Passages 38–41) accurately distinguishes their views from Baaij's position.
Qualifications and Textual Variants (Check #6): Addressed in Item 2 above.
No General Model Knowledge (Check #7): Verified. No external model knowledge was introduced into the audit or extractions.
